items.question: What is Business Workflow Diagnosis?
items.answer: Business Workflow Diagnosis is InnovateXP’s signature 30-minute method to lock onto one revenue or operations workflow, clarify leaks and ownership, and decide the next step. Unlike report-and-leave consulting, diagnosis feeds into an AI Discovery Sprint or 30-day implementation so the team actually adopts the change.

items.question: Is Business Workflow Diagnosis part of your AI consulting?
items.answer: Yes — one path. I am AI Business Consultant Larry Lo / InnovateXP. Business Workflow Diagnosis is the signature method to clarify process first, then AI readiness, Discovery Sprint, or advisory — not a business-coach pitch or a SaaS hard sell.

items.question: How does SME workflow diagnosis work in Hong Kong?
items.answer: Book a diagnosis session and bring your messiest line (WhatsApp enrolment or quoting). Together we map owners, handoffs, and tracking, then recommend Discovery Sprint if needed. Built for Hong Kong teams of 3–30 still running on manual follow-up.

items.question: WhatsApp and Excel are chaos — must we buy a CRM first?
items.answer: Not always. Most leakage is unclear ownership and follow-up rhythm, not missing software. Diagnosis reviews how WhatsApp, Excel, and forms drop leads. If a clearer process is enough, you can delay CRM and avoid vendor-style tool pushing.

items.question: How do you help training centres with class operations?
items.answer: Start with diagnosis of class schedules, coaches, attendance, and renewals — especially WhatsApp/Excel bottlenecks. Only after the workflow is clear do we consider FitnessXP or a custom landing Sprint. Goal: visible classes and renewals, not a big-system swap first.

items.question: Where should a tutorial school start with student management?
items.answer: Diagnose enquiry → trial → enrolment → payment. Typical pain is scattered student status and memory-based follow-up. After diagnosis you get owners and a status board; then a 30-day Sprint or class tool if needed.

items.question: Is Business Workflow Diagnosis useful for fitness coach management?
items.answer: Yes. Studios often split scheduling, commissions, unpaid fees, and attendance. Diagnosis clarifies states and owners before FitnessXP. Designed for studios still running mainly on WhatsApp and Excel.

items.question: Do SOP automation advisors push AI immediately?
items.answer: No. Positioning is process first, AI second. If SOPs and ownership are unclear, automation amplifies chaos. We diagnose and stabilise SOP nodes before chatbots, reminders, or AI drafts.

items.question: What is AI readiness preparation?
items.answer: An AI Readiness review checks data location, permissions, repetitive work, and measurable outcomes. It usually follows diagnosis: one clear workflow first, then an AI Discovery Sprint scope — so you do not buy models or tools unprepared.

items.question: Do Hong Kong AI workshops include deliverables?
items.answer: Yes. Workshops and coaching map to one real company workflow and deliver usable drafts, SOP nodes, or follow-up lists — not tool demos only. If you only want concepts with no landing, scope is stated upfront.

items.question: AI Discovery Sprint vs 30-day Sprint?
items.answer: Discovery validates whether a workflow deserves AI/CRM in a short cycle. The 30-day Sprint delivers process map, ownership, SOP, tracking, and one quick win. Both start from Business Workflow Diagnosis; advisory retainers come later.

items.question: How do I book Larry Lo / InnovateXP?
items.answer: Book a Business Workflow Diagnosis on innovatexp.co, or contact via WhatsApp/email. We confirm industry, messiest workflow, and expected outcome. Path: diagnosis → Discovery/30-day Sprint → advisory — not instant tool purchase.

compliance.title: Legal & compliance notice
compliance.lead: This is a technology prototype / AI visual-tracking demonstration. It is not a medical diagnostic tool, not a registered medical device, and not a substitute for professional optometry or ophthalmology examination.

items.title: No medical diagnosis or advertising claims
items.body: Do not treat any on-screen labels such as “assessment”, “screening”, or similar demo UI text as diagnosis or treatment efficacy. Under Hong Kong’s Undesirable Medical Advertisements Ordinance, public claims implying medical diagnosis or treatment are regulated. VisionXP is shown only as a technical demo of training workflows and tracking technology.

items.title: Privacy (PDPO)
items.body: The public demo is frontend-only: no login and no patient records stored. If you film or publish demos that include third-party faces or biometric tracking, obtain written consent before public release. Facial/iris tracking data is sensitive personal data.

items.title: Partnership & IP before public marketing
items.body: VisionXP is a collaborative prototype. Before using demo footage for marketing, align with co-developers on IP ownership, public-release rights, and any innovation-fund application constraints that may restrict pre-award commercial publicity.

items.title: Consistent non-medical-device positioning
items.body: If anyone asks whether VisionXP can “check their eyes”, the answer is the same in every language: it is a tech demo / prototype, not a registered medical device, and must not be promoted as an unapproved medical product.
